coverage: Find a table for the built-in L banquette that Angela likes (about 48 x 32 in, pill or boat shaped, on a pedestal) and say exactly how it sits. Nothing may collide; the walk from the kitchen to the dining room must stay at least 24 inches with the chairs pushed in; a banquette seat only counts if there are at least 9 inches between the back cushion and the table edge. Everything else is a trade-off measured against today's table. Priorities in order: the kitchen-to-dining walkway, room to slide into and sit on both benches, two comfortable everyday seats and four with guests, Angela's size and style, cost.

Polygon / layered furniture and exact circular arc geometry use flatten-js. Ellipses use 192-chord polygons (under 0.006-in radial error at 84 in); boat is an illustrative profile, not manufacturer CAD.
Bounded streamed search retains two fronts per family; not a proof of continuous optimality. Guide bands 24 / 30 / 36 in, chairs 24 hard and 32 / 36 / 44 preference; not code.

ranking_policy: filter invalid; cluster by (table shape and size class, long axis, overlap pattern, number of chairs); pick distinct representatives; rank EVERY shown layout (Today, generated, pinned, council) on one scale, lexicographically by bands: (1) walk to the dining room with a chair on the open side seated: 30+ comfortable, 24-30 tight, below 24 minimal; (2) reach from each bench used daily: table edge over the seat front by 0-4 in, or cushion-to-edge 9-13 in = comfortable; 13-15 = a lean; over 15 or a gap beyond the seat front = too far; under 9 = cramped; (3) Angela's preference: length 44-53 and width 28-34 with pill, boat, racetrack or oval shape and a pedestal or plate base = strong; one of those off = partial; round or rectangle under 40 long = weak; (4) style fit (walnut or warm oak, mid-century form); (5) seats at the table; (6) available without a custom quote; (7) lower cost. Show Today plus the top four distinct layouts first (any source; label council picks as such), then fold the rest under 'More options (n)'. Each card states its rank and one trade-off sentence.
